examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Track maximum keys and maximum child pointers separately: an internal node with k separator keys has k+1 children. On leaf split copy the new separator upward while retaining its data entry; an internal split generally promotes/removes a separator. Splits can propagate to the root and increase tree height.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A B+ tree internal node has 7 separator keys. How many child pointers does it have?

**Answer: 8.** Separators divide key space into one region before the first, six between keys, and one after the last: eight child intervals. Thus k keys require k+1=8 child pointers.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Minimum occupancy has a root exception. Split position conventions can differ; use the rule stated in the question when tracing exact keys.

Do not assume “order” always means maximum keys; use the question’s explicit convention.
